subject.title: Feature Request: Image batching / media group buffering at gateway layer

question: Should rapid media batching for channels without native grouping metadata be a LINE-owned opt-in feature, a broader shared channel/plugin contract, or intentionally unsupported?
rationale: The remaining request adds delayed webhook behavior and public configuration for a channel with no reliable grouping id, so automation should not choose the default, heuristic, or owner boundary.

options.title: LINE opt-in batching
options.body: Add a conservative LINE plugin config key and buffer same-account, same-conversation, same-sender downloadable media with documented latency and reply-token tradeoffs.

options.title: Shared channel contract
options.body: Design a media-aware SDK/core channel contract first, accepting broader compatibility review before changing LINE.

options.title: Keep unsupported
options.body: Keep native Telegram media-group handling only and document that channels without reliable grouping metadata dispatch media events individually.

recommendation.title: LINE opt-in batching
recommendation.body: Add a conservative LINE plugin config key and buffer same-account, same-conversation, same-sender downloadable media with documented latency and reply-token tradeoffs.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses LINE config, shared channel behavior, and repository config-surface policy where current blame and path history show the strongest routing signal.
